traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Urtica lyallii: stems 1 m to 2 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Urtica lyallii: leaves 3 cm to 15 cm long.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a tall herb forming dense patches of upright stems with opposite, coarsely toothed, heart-shaped leaves and hanging strings of tiny green flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.6 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark green leaves; green flower strings.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.inflorescence.note: The Flora of North America's account of the species, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): inflorescences paniculate, pedunculate, elongate; Jepson eFlora: spike-, raceme- or panicle-like, 1 to 7 cm, generally longer than the petiole.

traits.inflorescence_posture.note: Drooping clusters from the leaf axils and at the stem tips, as Pacific Northwest field guides and Portland State University's notes describe them, quoted in search results (the pages themselves were not read): read as nodding.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Each of its axillary clusters drawn flower by flower (spec rework L1c), its kind and its droop from its characters, by the rules at the flowering plants: a panicle about 6 cm long of 6 branches of 8 tiny green flowers, by eye (floras give no count), leaving the stem at about 60 degrees and bending over. From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): four green tepals in two pairs, four stamens and a one-carpelled pistil (staminate and pistillate flowers are drawn as one), from the characters of Urticaceae and Urtica by the rules at the flowering plants.
